summary: 1932 Forest Service live-in lookout on Rich Mountain, Madison County, NC; restored 2018 and unstaffed. Probably the same tower as us-nc-rich-mountain.

facts.design: 14 by 14 ft live-in cab with catwalk on a metal tower

access.note: Reached by a short side trail from the Appalachian Trail; a gravel road of about six miles from the Hot Springs side is usually closed in winter.

visit.trail_note: Gravel road of about six miles from the Hot Springs side, usually closed in winter; short side trail from the Appalachian Trail.

events.note: Erected by the Forest Service with a 14-by-14-foot live-in cab.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 2, 2008.
Restored by a partnership of the Forest Service, ATC, FFLA and Carolina Mountain Club; ribbon cutting November 19, 2018.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives a 30-foot metal tower; a travel guide gives 31 feet. The story says 30 feet, with the travel guide's figure noted.

A travel guide credits most of the money to the Appalachian Trail Conservancy's license-plate grant. The Smoky Mountain News credits the Forest Service with $101,158, the bulk of the cost. The story follows the newspaper.

corrections.current: us-nc-rich-mountain-2: Rich Mountain, Madison County, tnlandforms NCT144 at 35.92666,-82.80527, as a separate lookout
corrections.proposed: Same tower as us-nc-rich-mountain (NHLR US 727, 35.927190,-82.804910); merge the records and retire this one
corrections.why: Both entries are the 1932 Pisgah National Forest lookout in Madison County. The two positions are about 67 m apart, which is within the error of a list position.

sources.title: Rich Mountain Lookout Fire Tower, Hot Springs

notes_for_editor: Probable duplicate of us-nc-rich-mountain (NHLR US 727). The register position 35.927190,-82.804910 and the tnlandforms NCT144 position 35.92666,-82.80527 are about 67 m apart, with the same name, county, forest and 1932 build. Recommend merging into us-nc-rich-mountain and retiring this record and story; the content here can be dropped without losing anything. Conflicts: height 30 ft (register) vs 31 ft (travel guide); funding credit (travel guide vs newspaper). No condition report after the 2018 restoration was found. Not used: the 2017 public-access claim and the CCC-camp claim noted on the existing record, neither of which appeared in a page opened here.
